items.title: Exclude the project from `no-build` by default
items.reason: Canonical match: it asks for global `no-build` to protect external dependencies without blocking the first-party project, and its discussion specifically identifies VCS-derived dynamic versions as incompatible with that policy today.

items.title: `uv build --no-build` fails
items.reason: Earlier local-source-tree design discussion. A maintainer confirms that `no-build` currently covers local projects and says separating local source trees would require distinct policy; unlike the new issue, its direct reproduction uses build and sync rather than lock-time metadata.

items.title: Omit dynamic versions from the lockfile
items.reason: Historical partial support for dynamic project versions. The PR discussion explicitly confirms that locking still invokes the build backend, so the new result is not a regression of this fix.

related.search_scope: Exact searches covered `no-build`, `dynamic version`, setuptools-scm, the emitted source-distribution error, and `uv lock`; conceptual searches covered first-party and local source trees, static versus dynamic metadata, backend metadata preparation, and excluding the project from build policy. Fix-oriented searches inspected astral-sh/uv#9776 and astral-sh/uv#9785 for static metadata, plus astral-sh/uv#7533, astral-sh/uv#10622, and astral-sh/uv#11046 for dynamic lockfile history. astral-sh/uv#9776 was ruled out as the canonical match because its project metadata is fully static. astral-sh/uv#17487 was also inspected but concerns an external dependency whose dependency metadata requires backend execution.

type_reason: astral-sh/uv#17416 already tracks the same underlying capability: exempt the first-party project from global `no-build` so project operations can run its backend while dependency builds remain disabled. The new report adds a lock-specific setuptools-scm reproduction. This is not a regression of astral-sh/uv#10622; that pull request omitted dynamic versions from lockfiles but explicitly left backend invocation in place.
summary: astral-sh/uv#17416 is the canonical open issue. astral-sh/uv#12607 provides the earlier local-source-tree policy context, and merged astral-sh/uv#10622 documents why dynamic versions can be omitted from the lockfile while backend metadata preparation still occurs.
draft_response: Thanks for the minimal reproduction. This is the same underlying limitation tracked in astral-sh/uv#17416: `no-build` currently also blocks build-backend metadata preparation for the first-party project, while this dynamic version requires the backend during locking. astral-sh/uv#10622 added support for omitting dynamic project versions from the lockfile, but its discussion notes that locking still invokes the backend. We’ll use astral-sh/uv#17416 to track separating first-party project builds from dependency builds; your setuptools-scm example is a useful lock-specific reproduction.
